hook: Your GenAI system is built — now run it where the enterprise already lives. **Azure's AI stack is the most complete commercial offering on earth** — and this reel is the architect's map of it.

scenes.title: Azure OpenAI Service: GPT behind your enterprise boundary
scenes.sub: The same OpenAI models — with your tenancy, your keys, your compliance
scenes.narration: Azure OpenAI Service serves OpenAI's models — GPT-4o, o-series reasoning models, embeddings — through YOUR Azure subscription. The differences from the public API matter architecturally: DATA — prompts and completions don't train OpenAI models and live within your compliance boundary — the deal-breaker question for most enterprises is answered by tenancy alone; DEPLOYMENTS — you provision named deployments of specific model versions — 'my-gpt4o' pins a version, so an OpenAI model update never silently changes your app's behavior — the drift problem GA-04 warned about, solved at the platform level; and SCALE — tokens-per-minute quotas per deployment, not per account — you size quota like compute. The 2025 story is **Azure AI Foundry**: the portal around the models — model catalog (OpenAI, Llama, Mistral, Phi), prompt playgrounds, evaluation tools, tracing — one control plane for everything this reel covers. Architects pick Azure OpenAI for one reason: it's the fastest path from 'works in a notebook' to 'signed off by InfoSec'.

scenes.title: Calling your deployment — the SDK is nearly identical
scenes.body:
from openai import AzureOpenAI

client = AzureOpenAI(
    azure_endpoint="https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/",
    api_key=os.environ["AZURE_OPENAI_KEY"],   # or DefaultAzureCredential
    api_version="2024-12-01-preview",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="my-gpt4o",          # your DEPLOYMENT name, not the model name
    messages=[{"role": "user",
               "content": "Summarize this incident report: ..."}],
    temperature=0.2,
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

# Same SDK, same shape as the public API — swap the client
# and the prompt-engineering work from GA-03/GA-04 carries over.
annot: model= is your deployment name — the indirection that lets you version-swap without touching app code
api_version is explicit: Azure versions the REST contract — pin it, upgrade deliberately
Everything from GA-03 (prompting) and GA-04 (structured output) works unchanged — that's the point

scenes.title: Azure AI Search: RAG's missing half, as a managed service
scenes.sub: Vectors, hybrid, semantic ranker — GA-10's stack without the plumbing
scenes.narration: GA-10 built RAG retrieval by hand — embeddings, a vector store, a retriever. Azure AI Search offers the same as a service with three architecturally significant features. VECTORS — native vector fields with HNSW indexing — same pgvector mechanics GA-10 taught, minus the database ops; HYBRID — vector + full-text BM25 in ONE query — production truth from GA-10: pure vector search misses exact terms (IDs, error codes, names) and pure keyword misses semantics — hybrid gets both, and Search fuses the scores for you; and SEMANTANTIC RANKER — an LLM-based re-ranking pass over the top-N results — the reranker pattern GA-10 sketched, as a checkbox. Add integration: Azure OpenAI embeddings can be computed inside the ingestion pipeline, and the whole service is the retriever Azure's RAG templates assume. The architect's question isn't 'is it good' — it's 'do I want to operate pgvector myself, or buy retrieval as a service with a SLA'.

scenes.title: Hybrid retrieval in one query
scenes.body:
from azure.search.documents import SearchClient

results = search_client.search(
    search_text=query,                 # BM25 branch
    vector_queries=[VectorizedQuery(
        vector=embed(query), fields="content_vector")],
    query_type="semantic",             # LLM re-ranking pass
    top=5,
)

# One round-trip, three retrieval strategies fused:
#  1. keyword   — exact terms, IDs, error codes
#  2. vector    — semantic neighbors
#  3. semantic ranker — re-scores top 50 by meaning
# GA-10's hand-rolled pipeline, expressed as configuration.
annot: search_text + vector_queries = hybrid — the default choice, confirmed by GA-10's failure stories
query_type='semantic' is the reranker — expensive per call, applied only to the top candidates
top=5 then lands in the context window GA-10 sized — retrieval count is a context-budget decision

scenes.title: Document Intelligence & Content Safety: data in, harm out
scenes.sub: The two services guarding RAG's front door and the app's last line
scenes.narration: Two services bracket every production GenAI pipeline. DOCUMENT INTELLIGENCE — the ingestion side: PDFs, scans, forms, tables — layout-aware extraction that knows a table is a table — GA-09/GA-10's chunking quality is decided HERE: garbage extraction produces garbage chunks, and no retrieval tuning recovers it — read order, section headers, table structure preserved — it turns the messiest enterprise input — 20-year-old scanned PDFs — into clean structured text. CONTENT SAFETY — the output side: a screening service that classifies text and images across harm categories — hate, self-harm, sexual, violence — plus jailbreak and indirect-attack detection — it's AG-09's guardrail layer as a managed API: send the user input AND the model output, get severity scores and block/annotate decisions. Position it exactly where AG-09 drew the boundary: input screen before the LLM call, output screen before the user sees anything. Neither service replaces your guardrails logic — they replace you operating your own classifier fleet.

scenes.title: Dual screening with Content Safety
annot: Screen BOTH sides — AG-09's rule: input screening stops attacks, output screening stops harm
severity >= 2 is a tuning dial — like AG-09's thresholds, per-app and per-audience
Indirect prompt injection (AG-22) gets its own detector — screen retrieved documents too

scenes.title: Managed identity, private endpoints & the Copilot ecosystem
scenes.sub: The three answers InfoSec asks for — and where all this plugs into M365
scenes.narration: Three enterprise mechanics make Azure the default choice for .NET shops. MANAGED IDENTITY — your app proves WHO it is via the platform, not a secret in a config file — no API keys in app settings, no rotation runbooks — every call to Azure OpenAI, Search, or Storage rides the app's identity — AG-23's secrets discipline, enforced by the platform; PRIVATE ENDPOINTS — traffic from your VNet to Azure services never touches the public internet — the network diagram InfoSec wants is a closed loop; and the COPILOT ECOSYSTEM — Microsoft 365 Copilot is built on this same stack — which matters strategically: the data your app processes lives in SharePoint, Teams, Outlook — Microsoft's retrieval and grounding story for Copilot (Graph connectors) means YOUR RAG app and THEIR Copilot can share one search index and one compliance boundary. Architect takeaway: pick Azure when the enterprise already lives there — the integration tax of going elsewhere often exceeds the model premium.

scenes.title: Managed identity — no keys, anywhere
scenes.body:
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
from openai import AzureOpenAI

# The app proves its identity to Azure — nothing to leak,
# nothing to rotate. The endpoint URL isn't a secret.
credential = DefaultAzureCredential()

client = AzureOpenAI(
    azure_endpoint="https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/",
    azure_ad_token_provider=lambda: credential.get_token(
        "https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default"
    ).token,
    api_version="2024-12-01-preview",
)

# RBAC completes the picture: the app's identity gets
# 'Cognitive Services OpenAI User' on THIS deployment only
# — blast radius measured in one deployment, not one key.
annot: DefaultAzureCredential works locally (VS, az CLI) and in Azure (managed identity) — zero code difference
RBAC per deployment: a compromised app can only spend quota on what it was granted — AG-23's least privilege
The token provider pattern is the same shape as AG-23's credential helpers — secrets hygiene scales up

recap: Azure OpenAI = OpenAI models inside YOUR tenancy: version-pinned deployments, quota per deployment, data out of training — the InfoSec fast-track
Azure AI Search gives GA-10's whole retrieval stack as a service: vectors, hybrid BM25+vector fusion, and an LLM semantic ranker
Document Intelligence decides RAG quality at ingestion; Content Safety is AG-09's guardrail as an API — screen input AND output
Managed identity + private endpoints answer the three security questions before they're asked — and M365 Copilot shares the same stack

quiz.q: Why does the model parameter in an Azure OpenAI call take your deployment NAME (e.g. 'my-gpt4o') rather than the model name (e.g. 'gpt-4o')?
opts: Deployment names are required because Azure doesn't expose model names at all
The indirection pins a specific model version — you upgrade deployments deliberately instead of OpenAI silently changing your app's behavior
It's just a naming convention with no behavioral effect
The model name is a secret and must never appear in code
quiz.why: A named deployment is version-pinned. OpenAI can retire or update 'gpt-4o', but 'my-gpt4o' stays on what you deployed until YOU change it — GA-04's drift problem solved at the platform level.

quiz.q: In Azure AI Search, what does query_type='semantic' add on top of hybrid (text + vector) search?
opts: It converts the query to embeddings before searching
It encrypts the query for compliance
An LLM-based reranker pass that re-scores the top candidates by meaning — the reranker pattern GA-10 sketched, as configuration
It forces the search to use only the vector index
quiz.why: Semantic ranking is a second-stage reranker. Hybrid first-stage retrieval gets good candidates; the semantic ranker reorders them by deeper meaning — applied to top-N only because it's expensive per call.

quiz.q: Where do Document Intelligence and Content Safety sit in a production RAG pipeline?
opts: Both run after the LLM call, on the final answer only
Document Intelligence on the ingestion side (clean extraction before chunking); Content Safety screens both user input before the LLM and output before the user sees it
Document Intelligence is for output formatting; Content Safety is for input parsing
They are alternatives — you use one or the other, never both
quiz.why: Garbage extraction produces garbage chunks — no retrieval tuning fixes bad ingestion. And AG-09's boundary rule holds as a service: screen input to stop attacks, screen output to stop harm.

code.title: The Azure GenAI reference call
code.body:
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
from openai import AzureOpenAI

# Identity: managed identity — no keys in config
# Model: version-pinned deployment
# Data: inside your tenancy, never training
client = AzureOpenAI(
    azure_endpoint="https://my-resource.openai.azure.com/",
    azure_ad_token_provider=lambda: DefaultAzureCredential()
        .get_token("https://cognitiveservices.azure.com/.default").token,
    api_version="2024-12-01-preview",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="my-gpt4o",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": question}],
)
# Retrieval, safety, documents: sibling services on the
# same identity — one boundary, one compliance story.
annot: Three lines of identity plumbing replace an entire secrets-management runbook
Everything prompt-engineering from GA-03 onward ports unchanged — the SDK is the public one
This call is the 'hello world' GA-30's cost model prices

notes:
# Azure AI Services — architect's map

## The stack in one view
| Layer | Service | Replaces (our hand-built) |
|---|---|---|
| Models | Azure OpenAI / AI Foundry | public OpenAI API + model management |
| Retrieval | Azure AI Search | pgvector + retriever (GA-10) |
| Ingestion | Document Intelligence | PDF parsing, layout, tables |
| Safety | Content Safety | guardrail classifiers (AG-09) |
| Identity | Managed Identity + RBAC | API keys in config (AG-23) |
| Network | Private Endpoints | public API surface |

## Azure OpenAI vs public OpenAI API
- **Tenancy**: prompts/completions stay in your boundary; never train OpenAI models.
- **Deployments**: named, version-pinned; upgrades are deliberate.
- **Quota**: tokens-per-minute per deployment — size it like compute.
- **AI Foundry**: portal + SDK control plane — model catalog, playgrounds, eval, tracing.

## Azure AI Search
- Vectors (HNSW), hybrid text+vector with score fusion, semantic ranker (LLM re-rank top-N).
- Rule from GA-10 holds: hybrid is the production default; exact terms need BM25.

## Document Intelligence & Content Safety
- Extraction quality decides RAG quality. Scan → layout → tables → clean text.
- Screen input AND output (AG-09's boundary as an API). Indirect-injection detector for retrieved docs (AG-22).

## Enterprise mechanics
- Managed identity: no keys, no rotation; RBAC scoped per deployment.
- Private endpoints: no public traffic.
- M365 Copilot shares the stack — Graph connectors let your app and Copilot share indexes.

## Decision heuristic
Pick Azure when the enterprise already lives there. The integration tax of a separate vendor stack (identity, network, compliance sign-off) usually exceeds any model-price difference.
